pages.text: Rahina and her cousin Ameyaw filled a wide basin with clean water. “Which things will float?” asked Rahina. Beside the basin lay five small objects: a cork, a coin, a green leaf, a smooth stone, and a square of kitchen foil.
sentences: Rahina and her cousin Ameyaw filled a wide basin with clean water.
“Which things will float?” asked Rahina.
Beside the basin lay five small objects: a cork, a coin, a green leaf, a smooth stone, and a square of kitchen foil.
pages.alt: Rahina and Ameyaw kneeling beside a wide basin of clear water on a courtyard mat, with a cork, a coin, a green leaf, a pebble, and a flat square of silver foil beside them.

pages.text: First they guessed, and then they tested each one. The cork floated, and the leaf floated too. The coin sank, and the stone sank. Next, Ameyaw squeezed the foil into a tight little ball, and it sank to the bottom.
sentences: First they guessed, and then they tested each one.
The cork floated, and the leaf floated too.
The coin sank, and the stone sank.
Next, Ameyaw squeezed the foil into a tight little ball, and it sank to the bottom.
pages.alt: Close view of the clear water basin: the cork and green leaf float on top while the coin, smooth stone, and tightly balled silver foil rest on the bottom.

pages.text: Rahina had an idea. She folded a matching square of foil into a little boat with high sides. When she placed it gently on the water, it floated! “It is the same kind of foil,” said Ameyaw, “so why does it float now?”
sentences: Rahina had an idea.
She folded a matching square of foil into a little boat with high sides.
When she placed it gently on the water, it floated!
“It is the same kind of foil,” said Ameyaw, “so why does it float now?”
pages.alt: Rahina gently setting a neat little silver foil boat onto the water surface where it floats smoothly as Ameyaw watches in amazement.

pages.text: Rahina remembered what her teacher had explained. “A boat’s wide shape pushes aside plenty of water, and the water pushes back up,” she said. “The boat also holds air inside, so it stays light for its size.”
sentences: Rahina remembered what her teacher had explained.
“A boat’s wide shape pushes aside plenty of water, and the water pushes back up,” she said.
“The boat also holds air inside, so it stays light for its size.”
pages.alt: Close sunlit view of the hollow silver foil boat sitting high and buoyant on the sparkling water while Rahina cups her hands to explain its shape to Ameyaw.

pages.text: They placed small stones into the foil boat, one by one, counting together. On the eighth stone, water rushed in and the boat sank! “Every boat can carry only so much,” said Rahina. “That is why real boats have a safe load limit.”
sentences: They placed small stones into the foil boat, one by one, counting together.
On the eighth stone, water rushed in and the boat sank!
“Every boat can carry only so much,” said Rahina.
“That is why real boats have a safe load limit.”
pages.alt: Ameyaw adding a tiny pebble to the stone-filled silver foil boat just as it tips below the water surface while Rahina watches closely.

pages.text: Their mother smiled from her stool. “A basin is safe for testing, yet never play near a river or deep water without a grown-up,” she reminded them. Afterwards, the cousins wiped the floor dry and drew pictures of the floaters and sinkers.
sentences: Their mother smiled from her stool.
“A basin is safe for testing, yet never play near a river or deep water without a grown-up,” she reminded them.
Afterwards, the cousins wiped the floor dry and drew pictures of the floaters and sinkers.
pages.alt: Rahina and Ameyaw drying splashes around the basin with a cloth while their smiling mother sits nearby on her wooden stool.

activities.question: What was special about the foil boat?
options: It floated, even though the tight foil ball sank
It sank like a stone at once

activities.question: How many stones did the boat carry safely before it sank on the eighth?
activities.explanation: It sank when the eighth stone went in, so it carried seven stones safely.
